_design_note:
C51 (Bellemare et al. 2017): predict the distribution of the return over 51 fixed atoms instead of its mean. Declared as route R02_10 rather than as an algorithm field because C51 changes the head's output shape and its loss together -- 6 numbers become 6x51 probabilities and Huber becomes cross-entropy -- and that pair is what C51 is. Everything else is R02_9's: handcrafted_v3, (128, 64), Double DQN action selection on the expectation, Adam, clip 10, n-step 5, the same replay block, E02 and L01.

The support is measured, not chosen for roundness. R02_9's own batch-mean TD targets run from -0.29 to 3.57 across 14,699 training rounds, and a single target reaches roughly 12 when a five-step window collects coins and a kill together. [-2, 12] over 51 atoms puts the resolution (0.28) where the mass is and leaves the tails inside the grid.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: The value head: scalar Q with Huber loss -> categorical distribution over 51 atoms on [-2, 12] with cross-entropy. Route R02_9 -> R02_10, which differ in network and td_loss and nothing else.
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/m3_lr_decay_5000_vs3rb_20260827/ (R02_9), ten repeats of the holdout classic_versus_opponents suite: score 3.6371, sd 0.1214, coins_share 0.3449. This arm's config is that config with one field changed.
_predeclared_design_numbers.cost: Measured: 482 us per gradient step against the scalar head's 259, so 4.1 minutes against 2.2 over a 5000-round arm's 513,000 gradient steps. The game simulation dominates either way.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Indistinguishable from R02_9 over ten repeats closes distributional value estimation on this line.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: A richer per-step training signal, which on Atari is worth more than any other single Rainbow component. The returns here are genuinely bimodal -- a round ends either in a death or in a collection run -- which is the shape a mean squashes and a distribution keeps. Stated honestly: this is a prediction about the learning signal, not a mechanism aimed at any gap this line has measured.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training-seed distributions, coins_share and suicides beside every score, and the learning curve on the loot-crate primary suite. Every score names its scenario and whether opponents were present.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: Two arms measured once each need a gap of 0.246 on the tournament suite (section 7.20.2). The quoted comparison is ten repeats per arm of the same fifteen holdout jobs, Welch, |t| > 2.3.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_confound_this_arm_cannot_remove: A categorical head has more parameters than a scalar one, and no version of C51 does not. The trunk is identical -- 62 -> 128 -> 64 is R02_9's, unchanged -- but the output layer is 64 x 306 instead of 64 x 6, so the model holds 35,712 parameters against 16,512. Section 7.24.1 found width interacts with step size on this line, so a difference here is 'the distributional head', not 'distributional learning as such', and must be reported that way. The cheap follow-up if this arm wins is a scalar R02_9 with a wider final layer, which separates the two; there is no point running that control unless it wins.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_mechanism_check: Two ways this head fails quietly, both checked rather than assumed. First, the support: if the projected targets pile up on the first or last atom, the grid is clipping and the arm measures the grid rather than C51. Second, mean_target is reported as the expectation of the projected distribution, so it is comparable with every scalar arm's mean_target and a divergence shows up in the same number it always did.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_metric_that_decides_it: Official score on classic + 3 rule_based_agent, holdout seeds, ten repeats. That is the competition setting and the only promotion metric.
